title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Opening of a section titled 'Quelques calculs d'homotopie', apparently preparing explicit simplicial models for the divided-power de Rham complex project.

Setup. Let k be a commutative base ring. Grothendieck defines the simplicial k-module L_* : I ↦ k^I, i.e. [n] ↦ k^{n+1}, the functions on the vertices of Δ^n. Face maps are restriction of functions (∂_j forgets vertex j), so I ↦ k^I is contravariant and gives a simplicial object. The constant functions give a diagonal map k_* → L_* from the constant simplicial module. Set Ψ_* = L_*/k_*, with Ψ_n = k^{n+1}/k ≅ k^n, which is free.

Proposition 1: L_* is simplicially homotopy equivalent to 0. Proof via the Dold–Puppe (Dold–Kan) correspondence: it suffices that the normalized complex N(L)_n = {x ∈ L_n | ∂_1x = … = ∂_nx = 0} is contractible.
- For n ≥ 2, every coordinate lies in a face omitting some vertex j ≥ 1, so N_n = 0.
- N_1 = {(0, x_1)} ≅ k and N_0 = k.
- ∂_0 : N_1 → N_0 is the identity.
So N(L) is k → k by the identity, which is contractible.

Corollary 1.1: for any functor F : Mod(k) → C, F(L_*) (applied degreewise) is homotopic to the constant F(0). Simplicial homotopies are combinatorial, so any functor preserves them. In particular Λ^i L_*, Γ^i L_* and Sym^i L_* are contractible for i > 0, and equal k_* for i = 0.

Corollary 1.2: from the exact sequence 0 → k_* → L_* → Ψ_* → 0 we get π_i(Ψ) ≅ π_{i-1}(k_*), which is k for i = 1 and 0 otherwise. So Ψ_* is a K(k,1); indeed N(Ψ) is k placed in degree 1.

Corollary 1.3: π_j(Λ^i Ψ_*) = k for j = i and 0 otherwise, so Λ^i(L_*/k_*) is a K(k,i). The implied argument uses the Koszul-type exact sequence 0 → Λ^{i-1}Ψ → Λ^i L → Λ^i Ψ → 0, valid because the kernel k is free of rank 1. Since Λ^i L is contractible for i ≥ 1, this gives π_j Λ^i Ψ ≅ π_{j-1} Λ^{i-1} Ψ, and one inducts.

Since Ψ_n is free, Λ^i Ψ computes LΛ^i(k[1]). The result is therefore the instance M = k of the décalage LΛ^i(M[1]) ≃ LΓ^i(M)[i]. The purpose is to have explicit, functorial models of K(k,i), built from the 'linear functions on simplices' module, compatible with Λ, Γ and Sym. These would serve the comparison between divided-power structures and simplicial/de Rham constructions (cf. the previous page on DP(K^·) and the normalization functor ND).
errors: The argument for Cor. 1.3 is only sketched ('On conclut de ceci'); the needed exact sequence 0→Λ^{i-1}Ψ→Λ^iL→Λ^iΨ→0 is not written, though it is standard.
Cor. 1.1 needs 'homotopic' in the sense of simplicial homotopy equivalence, which is what Dold–Puppe gives. This is fine but implicit.
Corollaries 1.1–1.3 are proved here only for Λ^i. No analogous computation for Γ^i(Ψ) or Sym^i(Ψ) is given; Sym^i of K(k,1) is trivial for i≥2, while Γ^i is nontrivial.

deep.surprise_reason: Clean, correct but standard computations: contractibility via normalized complex and the rank-one case of the Illusie–Quillen décalage, with a neat explicit model. Nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'anneau de base (commun)' should read 'anneau de base (commutatif)'.
'complexe de dimension associé' is likely 'complexe normalisé associé' (hard to read); the defined object is the normalized Moore complex.
In Cor. 1.1 the added parenthetical lists the analogous objects Γ^i_k L_*, Sym^i_k L_* and their values Γ^i(0), Sym^i(0); the crossed-out line is the Γ^i variant.
Cor. 1.2: the crossed-out bracket remark reads roughly '[En fait, on a (Ψ^!_*) = complexe réduit à k placé en degré 1]', followed by a struck reference to the Dold–Puppe theorems.
